what: The value of the DSP's `@10` - data 0x0390 - read on the live board
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2, idle and on hook
why: `lar ar0, @10` immediately precedes each `cmpr eq` that gates the DSP's mailbox poll. With the NDX side effect measured as active (artifacts/ndx-probe-01), that instruction sets ARCR from @10 on every pass, so @10 is what the gate actually compares against.
resolving @10: Direct addressing is DP-relative. `ldp #007` sits immediately before the `lar ar0, @10` at 0x8105 and 0x810d, and the steady-state loop passes the `ldp #007` at 0x80e6 on every turn, so DP = 7 and @10 is data 0x0390 - not the memory-mapped AR0 at data 0x0010 that a DP = 0 reading would give.
what 0x0390 is: AR7's save slot. `sar ar7, @10` at 0x808f and 0x81a1 store it; `lar ar7, @10` at 0x80c5 and 0x8192 restore it. So the compare at 0x80d1 tests the live ring pointer against its own saved value.
control: artifacts/dsp-at10-control-01: the same kernel on data 0xffff returned 0x0083 sixteen times, matching artifacts/dsp-boot-word-01. So the probe reads live cells correctly and the zero is a reading, not a broken path.
caveats: Read with the modem idle and on hook, and read after the monitor has reset the DSP - so this is the value the resident left behind, not a sample of the running steady state.

It does not follow that @10 is zero during a call. The DSP's task and ring machinery may only be set up once a connection starts, and that state cannot be captured this way because arming the monitor takes the modem over.
A zero here is consistent with the harness's own observation that the gated block runs once during initialisation and then never again.
